name: Unhoused Services Ad Hoc Committee Liaison Meeting Agenda
minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Unhoused Services Ad Hoc Committee
  Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Friday, January 26, 2024
  2:00 PM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  January 26, 2024 / 2:00 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Mayor Julian Gold, Councilmember Lili Bosse, City Manager Nancy Coffey,
  Director of Community Services Stephanie Harris, Human Services
  Administrator Christopher Paulson, Human Servies Outreach Manager
  Enisha Clark, Human Services Specialist Susana De La Torre, Fire Chief
  Gregory Barton

  1) Public Comment:

  None

  2) Update on Enhanced Services to the Unhoused & Scattered Site Housing Program
  with Step Up on Second:
  a. Since beginning operation on November 15, 2022, the centralized 24-hour hotline
  has received a total of 860 calls and 21 emails.
  i. BH Public Works Customer Service has responded to 429 of those calls,
  due to them occurring during business hours on weekdays, with the
  remaining 431 calls being handled by Nastec at all other hours.
  b. The Apricot 360 system includes BH Ambassadors, BHOT, Park Rangers, PD
  MHET, Nastec, and Human Services for a total of 56 users. This is currently being
  expanded to include the Nurse Practitioners Program at the Fire Department.
  i. Outreach Staff have had 14,507 encounters with 1,471 individuals.
  ii. Individuals have either requested or accepted service from BHOT in 1,134
  encounters.
  iii. The top locations for encounters were at the Parks, Library, and Beverly
  Gardens Park which had 3,146, 2,026, and 1,690 encounters respectively.
  c. In 2022 the contract with Step Up on Second for the Beverly Hills Outreach Team
  (BHOT) was expanded from 3 members working 5 days a week to 5 members
  working 7 days a week.
  i. Since 2015 BHOT has placed 26 individuals into permanent & supportive
  housing, 61 individuals into one of the 5 contacted PATH beds, and 35
  individuals have been reunited with their families through the home again
  program. 8 of the people served by the home again program was served
  during the first 7 months of 2023. This data is from before the
 Highlights for January 26, 2024
Unhoused Services Ad Hoc Committee

  implementation of the Permanent Supportive Housing Program in
  November of 2023.
  d. The Beverly Hills Police Department Mental Health Evaluation Team (MHET) was
  formed by a partnership between the city and the LA County Department of Mental
  Health to bring 2 licensed clinical social workers to the city where they would be
  paired with 2 police officers.
  i. BHPD created their half of the MHET team in April 2023, with the County
  workers arriving in September 2023.
  ii. The team has had 1033 contacts with individuals, of which 872 were
  unhoused. They have also conducted 555 footbeats, 43 arrests, 90 5150
  Holds/Voluntary Transports with 74 of the 90 individuals being unhoused,
  and 7 HOME Team referrals.
  e. In August 2023, the City Council authorized a 10-year agreement with step up on
  second for 30 units of permanent supportive housing, up to 280 nights annually of
  motel stays for interim short-term housing, and case management and individual
  rehabilitative services.
  f. The number of encounters per person is due to how long it takes to build trust
  between outreach teams and homeless individuals.
  g. The 3 parks where homeless individuals were encountered most often were La
  Cienega, followed by Roxbury, followed by Will Rodgers.
  h. Encounters tend to happen more often in the summer months, due to both
  increased numbers of tourists who call the hotline as well as increased numbers
  of homeless individuals entering the city.
  i. An encounter can just be a conversation between staff and an individual. Most
  encounters do not leave this stage.
  j. Now that we have housing options due to Step Up on Second, the city needs to
  increase the level of code enforcement. These code violations will eventually lead
  to an arrest, following which the city prosecutor and city staff will push for it to go
  to a homeless court, where the city will argue for sentencing to be mandatory
  treatment rather than jailtime.
  k. The constant interaction with homeless individuals is necessary in order to
  pressure them into accepting services and eventually treatment, and Human
  Services staff points to this constant interaction as one of the reasons for the low
  homeless population of the city.
  l. The large number of contacts is also necessary to successfully refer someone to
  the HOME Team.
  m. 12 of the 30 Step Up on Second beds have been filled since the signing of the
  contract.

  3) Homelessness Plan:
  a. The plan was developed in conjunction with Bevely Hills Staff, Abby Arnold, and
  Jenny Swan.
  b. The development of this plan involved extensive outreach between January and
  August of 2023:
  i. Outreach efforts included 28 meetings and interviews with stakeholders
  such as city commissions, business groups, faith communities, city
  departments, and Council members.
 Highlights for January 26, 2024
Unhoused Services Ad Hoc Committee

  c. A survey was conducted between the months of May and August 2023 using a
  citywide mailer and social media posts which had 853 residents respond, as well
  as 46 city employees.
  d. The themes from the outreach efforts were that there were safety concerns for
  both residents and visitors, fear of interaction with someone experiencing either
  extreme mental health or drug issues, health and sanitation concerns, empathetic
  concerns, and quality of life concerns.
  e. Best practices are street medicine for health issues, a dedicated police detail for
  homelessness and mental health issues such as MHET, consistent outreach
  efforts by a consistent group of people to build trust, and high levels of coordination
  between the different departments, contractors, and government agencies.
  f. Recommendations.
  i. Strengthen the coordination between city departments and city-funded
  entities.
  1. Assign a single person as the lead coordinator for homelessness
  efforts in the city.
  2. Joint training efforts between different teams.
  3. Add another licensed social worker to Human Services staff so that
  one social worker can spend 100% of their time on the homeless.
  ii. Ensure community safety.
  1. Continue coordinating with County mental health resources.
  2. Continue collecting and analyzing data on homelessness.
  3. Consider expanding street medicine and park rangers to 24/7
  operation.
  iii. Maximize the effectiveness of Police and Fire responses.
  iv. Educate community members about how to connect with city services.
  1. Consider hiring a PR firm to communicate with residents on how to
  react when dealing with a homeless person. Also consider using
  Fire or PD to distribute this information.
  v. Improve and expand regional homeless services.
  vi. Prevent homelessness among Beverly Hills residents.
  g. County DA has directives not to prosecute trespassing or simple possession of
  drugs.
  h. BHPD will still cite individuals in violation of the laws that the DA chooses not to
  prosecute.
  i. In 2023 LAHSA stopped releasing data for the homeless population at an individual
  city level, instead releasing it by LA County supervisorial district, LA city, and by
  LA City Council District. The other 87 cities in LA county do not have access to the
  information on their individual homeless population.
  j. The 2024 LAHSA homeless count for Beverly Hills from 2 days prior to the meeting
  is unable to be disclosed due to an NDA, and it is not released in the final version
  due to the algorithm used not being able to generate an accurate homeless per
  square mile calculation for the individual cities.
  k. The LAHSA homeless count is a point in time count that occurs at night, which
  misses most of the city’s homeless population, who are transitory and come on
  buses during the day and leave at night.
 Highlights for January 26, 2024
Unhoused Services Ad Hoc Committee

  l. City staff have found the Apricot numbers to be far more useful at understanding
  the homeless population than the LAHSA count.
  m. The mayor has indicated that city staff should not cooperate with future LAHSA
  count operations should we be placed under a similar NDA for future counts.
  n. Should council decide to move forward with the entire plan, it would be a slow
  rollout to implement all the recommendations.

  4) Homelessness Plan Implementation Requests & Recommendations:
  a. The job qualification for the positions recommended in 1.D is that a candidate must
  be a licensed clinical social worker.
  b. To upgrade the contract with Step Up on Second, it would cost $121,194.00 for
  the rest of FY 2023-2024, and would cost $227,643.00 for FY 2024-2025.

  5) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: January 26, 2024 / 3:28 PM
